title: Card support execution record entry
description: One entry of the execution record: the system's own trace, its audit log, and the evaluation's source (ADR-0004, A turn, end to end; OPS-02). A turn is one run: it opens with turn_opened, holds its model calls, tool calls, controls, and reply, and closes with turn_closed. A turn that runs the graph writes one decision entry for each request it served, in order, the last of them just before turn_closed and before the run's last event; a warm-up runs no graph, so it writes none. Entries are keyed by the sign-in, then by the turn's start and the entry's sequence, so a sign-in's entries read in order. Text is masked before it is recorded (POL-11). The sign-in is Cognito's origin_jti, the handoff's session_id.

entry_key.description: The sort key: the turn's start on the wall clock, the turn's ID, and the entry's sequence, joined by #.

turn_id.description: Drawn by the entrypoint; never the client's run ID.

source.description: From the token's groups; every metric is split by it, so evaluation runs never pass for live traffic (EVL-13).

case_id.description: The evaluation case, for source evaluation only.

expires_at.description: Epoch seconds, 90 days after the entry, for DynamoDB's time to live (OPS-10).

origin_jti.description: The sign-in: Cognito's origin_jti, the policy's session (POL-09). It chooses the sandbox overlay a tool reads and writes.

bank_date.description: A date on the bank's own clock (POL-19).

bank_timestamp.description: A timestamp on the bank's own clock, naive, as the snapshot delivers it.

clock.description: The frozen bank's clock, published with the tools' data (ADR-0004, Two clocks). Today is the business date, and every window ends at the as-of instant.

hash.description: The first 16 hexadecimal digits of a SHA-256.

masked_text.description: Text the customer typed, masked by the entrypoint before anything stores it (POL-11).

reference.description: A handoff's reference: eight characters of Crockford's base32, in two groups of four (ADR-0007).

validation_error.description: A path and the rule it broke, never the value (POL-11).

wait_ms.description: On an attempt after the first: how long it waited before it was made.

waited_for.description: On an attempt after the first: what set the wait, the provider's retry-after, a jittered backoff, or nothing, for output that didn't parse (decision 18).

turn_opened_entry.description: A turn's first entry, stamped with everything that shapes it. Only the entrypoint opens turns: the deadline handoffs of ADR-0004's decision 7 are deferred, and building them would add a turn the deadline Lambda opens, with no runtime session or client IDs.

thread_key.description: The thread's key, derived from sub and the client's thread ID (decision 12).

oneOf.description: A control's answer, or a message typed while a control was pending (masked).

language.description: The conversation's language when the turn opens (POL-50).

app.description: The commit that last changed the deployed code (src/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock), so a commit that changes only documents or infrastructure deploys the same Runtime.

prompts.description: Each model node's prompt, by the hash of its text.

request_refused_entry.description: A request the entrypoint turned away before opening a turn; it is its own turn's only entry. The regression tests on threads and runtime sessions check these (ADR-0004).

errors.description: For invalid_request: where the request failed the chat contract, by the JSON Schema keyword that failed, or by one of the entrypoint's own checks: notNew (the last message is one the thread's checkpoint holds), notPending (a resume that doesn't answer the thread's pending control), or conflict (a message with a resume, or a warm-up with either).

model_call_entry.description: One attempt at one model call (decision 18). The reply's text is recorded by the reply entry, once checked.

provider.description: Null when no provider ran: the deterministic baseline or the scripted models (ADR-0005).

model_returned.description: The model_name the provider returned; null when the call failed.

outcome.description: connection_error: the request never reached the provider. Every outcome but ok and error is tried again, up to three attempts within the turn's deadline (decision 18, as amended on 2026-10-01).

usage.description: From usage_metadata; output tokens include reasoning. Null where the provider reports none.

cost_usd.description: At the provider's list price on the call's date; null when the price isn't known.

output.description: The structured output of a routing or extraction call that succeeded. A reply's or a handoff's text isn't kept here.

oneOf.description: The router: every supported request it finds, whether the message holds one at all (S5), whether it is a complaint (POL-44; ADR-0004's amendment of 2026-09-30), which language the message is mostly in (POL-50, POL-51; the amendment of 2026-10-02), and what a message with no request is, which chooses its fixed reply (POL-06; the amendment of 2026-10-03).
An extraction, each field among the values its step allows.

tool_call_entry.description: One attempt at one tool call. ok, not_found, refused, and invalid_input are the tool's own outputs, kept whole as its result; failed is a call the Lambda never answered, and denied is Cedar's JSON-RPC -32002 (POL-49). A handoff's evidence names these calls by call_id, with ok, not_found, and refused as ok, invalid_input and failed as error, and denied as denied.

via.description: gateway for the reads and the block; direct for file_handoff, which the Runtime invokes with IAM (ADR-0004, Where the tools run).

attempt.description: A call's attempts share its call_id; only a failed attempt is tried again, never a denied one (POL-48, POL-49).

request_id.description: The Gateway's request ID, or the Lambda's for a direct call; null when the call never reached either.

input.description: The tool's input as sent. For file_handoff, only the handoff's ID: the payload is in the case, and the forwarded token is never recorded.

result.description: The tool's output, whole, for ok, not_found, refused, and invalid_input. The grader checks each handoff fact against it (ADR-0005).

planned.description: The failure was a fault plan's, answered by the tool before it read anything, not a real timeout, throttle, or Lambda error (ADR-0004's amendment of 2026-10-01).

interrupt_entry.description: The controls a turn ended waiting on (POL-36, POL-45).

resume_entry.description: An answer to a pending control, and whether the graph took it. A stale control changes nothing and says why (POL-09, POL-36, POL-45).

refusal.description: Why an answer was not taken: the ID isn't the thread's pending one, the confirmation expired, or the answer came from another sign-in.

confirmation_entry.description: A change in a confirmation record's status, copied from the record, which expires after 24 hours (ADR-0004, The confirmation).

attempts.description: The block's writes under this confirmation, when it was consumed (POL-37).

block_outcome.description: Whether the read-back showed Blocked, when it was consumed.

reply_check_entry.description: The reply check's verdict on one part of a reply the model wrote (decision 8, as amended on 2026-10-01): one entry per part. Failures are named by rule, never by the text that broke them; missing_fact is a fact the part's fixed reply states and the model's left out.

fell_back.description: The reply was replaced by a fixed one built from the same facts.

reply_entry.description: The reply as the chat received it: checked, with its facts and outcomes filled in.

fixed_texts.description: The fixed sentences code added, by name: an action's outcome, a handoff's reference, a fallback (AI-05, POL-37, POL-45).

handoff_entry.description: A handoff saved as a draft, filed, or found already filed when a retry files it again. A draft is saved when the confirm control shows a handoff POL-38 or POL-39 may require; with decision 7 deferred, the Runtime files it when the confirmation ends within a turn, and otherwise it expires unfiled.

flagged.description: Parts of the payload failed validation after the fallback and were left out (ADR-0004, The handoff).

decision_entry.description: The turn's outcome, which the evaluation's scripted customer reacts to, never the reply's prose (ADR-0005). outcome_class names the path the turn is on, and awaiting what it ended waiting for: which card, a reason, which listed transaction, or a control. A turn that shows the confirm control is block, awaiting it; the turn a confirm resumes is block when the read-back verifies it, and hand_off when it doesn't (POL-37) or when POL-39 requires a handoff all the same; a cancelled or lapsed confirmation's reply is answer, or hand_off when POL-39 requires one; clarify is kept for which card, a reason, or which transaction (ADR-0005, as amended on 2026-10-02). A turn that serves several requests (POL-05) writes one entry per request, in order: each names the labels still queued after it, and only the last carries what the turn awaits, the others awaiting none (ADR-0004 and ADR-0005, as amended on 2026-10-01).

request_label.description: The request this turn served; null for a message with no card request (POL-06).

pending_labels.description: The requests still queued after this one, in POL-05's order.

rules.description: The rules that decided the outcome.

latency_ms.description: From the turn's opening to its last event.
